name: Linear (OAuth 2.0)
summary: Create an OAuth2 application in Linear, send users to linear.app/oauth/authorize with state and PKCE, exchange the code at api.linear.app, and call the GraphQL API. Generated live by the research agent from Linear's developer docs; nothing here was exercised in a Linear workspace.

active.basis: No hands-on run, so no effort figure is claimed.

wait.basis: The OAuth page checked describes no review step before users can authorize. Listing in Linear's Integration Directory was not researched.

prerequisites.text: A Linear workspace to own the app. Linear suggests a dedicated workspace, because every admin there can manage the app.

source.quote: It is highly recommended you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access.

steps.title: Create the OAuth2 application and its callback URLs
steps.detail: In Linear, open Settings → API and create an OAuth2 application. Add your agent application's backend callback (e.g. https://your-agent.example/auth/linear/callback, illustrative). Leave client credentials tokens off unless you need server-to-server tokens.

settings.explain: Illustrative production value. The redirect_uri you send later must be one of these. Localhost support was not established.
Only for server-to-server automation without a user; those tokens act as the app across public teams.

source.quote: Create a new OAuth2 Application and configure the redirect callback URLs to your application.

steps.title: Decide who actions appear to come from
steps.detail: Default actor=user makes changes as the authorizing person. For an agent, actor=app makes changes appear as your app instead.

source.quote: To enable the actor authorization, add actor=app parameter to your OAuth authorization URL.

steps.title: Request the narrowest scopes
steps.detail: read is always included. Prefer targeted scopes such as issues:create or comments:create over write, and avoid admin unless it is truly needed.

source.quote: read - (Default) Read access for the user’s account. This scope will always be present.

steps.title: Send the user to Linear with state and PKCE
steps.detail: GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope, state, and code_challenge with code_challenge_method=S256.

source.quote: Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied.

steps.title: Check state on the callback
steps.detail: Linear returns code and your state. Reject the callback if state differs from what you stored for this user.

source.quote: If the values do not match, the request should not be trusted.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
steps.detail: POST a form-encoded body with code, redirect_uri, client_id, client_secret, grant_type=authorization_code (and code_verifier if you used PKCE). Keep the client secret server-side.

source.quote: After receiving the code , you can exchange it for a Linear API access token: POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/token

steps.title: Call the GraphQL API with the token
steps.detail: Send Authorization: Bearer <access token> to https://api.linear.app/graphql, or pass the token to the Linear SDK client.

steps.title: Refresh tokens every day
steps.detail: Access tokens last 24 hours. Exchange the refresh token at the same token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token and store the new refresh token each time.

source.quote: The access token is valid for 24 hours and will need to be refreshed when it expires.

steps.title: Revoke tokens when a user disconnects
steps.detail: POST the token to the revoke endpoint using the token field; 200 means revoked.

gaps.text: Nothing was exercised in a Linear workspace; every step is documentation-backed only.
gaps.next_action: Create a test app in a throwaway workspace and run one read-only authorization.

gaps.text: Whether localhost callback URLs are accepted is not stated on the pages checked.
gaps.next_action: Try a loopback callback during a hands-on test.

gaps.text: Listing in Linear's Integration Directory and any review it involves were not researched.
gaps.next_action: Read Linear's integration directory guidelines before public launch.

verification.method: plain HTTPS fetch, tags stripped, normalized text match
